title: the Ninefold Court Rising Revisited
premise: When the border wards of Cinderfall collapse and the stars vanish in the same night, royal food-taster Freya Galloway discovers his seven years of slow-poison immunity and black-market charmwork have made him the only person who can walk unharmed into the Ninefold Court beneath the mountain. There he learns his own soul was sold to the court as a child, and that the dying dragon-fire keeping both worlds lit is fed by stolen souls, including that of his lost sister. Bargaining with exiled magicians, a disgraced ward-keeper, and the court's own renegade steward, Freya must steal back what was sold before the last flame gutters out. In the end he frees the souls by offering the court his immunity itself, relighting the fire at the cost of his protection and his old identity, and returns to a city that must now decide whether magic is crime or neighbor.
about_author: Yara Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing legal records of outlawed trades before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people whose survival depends on skills the law refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Freya. A night in the palace kitchens: Freya tastes for poison, palms a charm to a scullery maid, and counts his small savings. We learn his rules—never cast, never be seen, never hope. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Small Sins
chapters.summary: POV Freya, flashback braided with present. How an orphan boy learned charmwork from a hedge-witch, sold his first spell at twelve, and took the taster's post to build immunity against a court that hates magic. Beat: tenderness for the self he had to bury.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Mid-tasting, every star vanishes; the border wards fall with a sound like breaking glass. The palace erupts; Freya's hidden charms flare visibly for the first time. Beat: terror and exhilaration as his secret becomes public.

chapters.title: Arrested by the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Captain Ilsa Vane, ward-keeper turned investigator. She arrests three suspects including Freya, but her instruments read him as 'already dead inside'—a soul-mark she has seen only on court-taken children. Beat: cold duty cracking into doubt.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Interrogating Freya, she reveals the wards didn't keep magic out—they kept something beneath the mountain from reaching up. The city's founders sold it a price long ago. Beat: the vertigo of inherited guilt.

chapters.title: The Steward Below
chapters.summary: POV Freya. A summons arrives through his own pocket-charm: the court's renegade steward, Maren, offers truth if he comes down willingly. He escapes custody with Ilsa reluctantly following. Beat: choosing the unknown over the cell.

chapters.title: Descent by Dragon-Light
chapters.summary: POV Freya. The road under the mountain, lit by guttering veins of dragon-fire. Maren shows him the Ninefold Court's nine thrones, eight empty, one occupied by something wearing a king's shape. Beat: awe curdling to dread.

chapters.title: A Soul on the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Maren opens the court's ledger: Freya's name, sold at age five by the orphanage, payment for the city's founding charter. His immunity isn't talent—it's the court returning interest on its property. Beat: identity shattered.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was Also Sold
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Following Freya down, Ilsa finds records of a second child sold the same night: Freya's sister Bryn, whose soul now feeds the central flame. Beat: grief arriving ahead of understanding.

chapters.title: Ninefold Bargains
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Brought before the throne, Freya bargains using his taster's skill—he alone can identify which of nine offered cups carries the court's true oath. He wins audience rights but owes a favor unnamed. Beat: victory that feels like a trap.

chapters.title: The Fire That Eats Names
chapters.summary: POV Maren. The steward explains the dragon-fire runs on souls; each soul burned erases a name from the world's memory. Bryn is nearly spent. Maren's own treachery: she wants the fire out entirely. Beat: moral vertigo between two ruinous choices.

chapters.title: Charmwork in Earnest
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Seven years of tiny illegal spells become one act of open magic: Freya crafts a vessel to carry a soul without burning it. It fails twice, nearly killing him—his immunity absorbing the backlash. Beat: craft finally meaning something.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Ordered by the regent to seal the mountain and let the court starve, Ilsa instead burns her warrant. Justice outside the law begins here. Beat: quiet, costly defiance.

chapters.title: The Empty Throne Room
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya infiltrates the flame-chamber during the court's long vigil, finds Bryn's ember small as a candle-flame—and meets the thing on the throne face to face. It claims to remember him fondly. Beat: horror wearing intimacy.

chapters.title: What the Court Wants Back
chapters.summary: POV Freya. The court reveals its price for Bryn: not a soul but a body—a living taster immune to its fire, to serve forever. Freya pretends to consider. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Maren's Treason
chapters.summary: POV Maren. The steward moves early to smother the flame, which would free all souls but plunge both worlds into dark. Freya and Ilsa must stop their ally to save the light. Beat: allies at cross-purposes, no villains.

chapters.title: The Last Gutter
chapters.summary: POV Freya. The flame drops to embers as factions collide in the chamber. Freya pours his stolen years of immunity—the court's own investment in him—into the fire as substitute fuel. Beat: sacrifice of the self he built.

chapters.title: Bryn, Remembered
chapters.summary: POV Freya. The vessel works: Bryn's soul lifts free, whole, and speaks his childhood name—the only proof he ever had a family. But the court convulses, demanding repayment. Beat: joy inseparable from debt.

chapters.title: The Ninth Throne
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Climax. Rather than serve or flee, Freya sits the ninth empty throne and dissolves the founding contract with the one power the court never priced: consent freely given. The court unmakes its kingship; the mountain exhales. Beat: triumph through surrender.

chapters.title: Ascension Without Stars
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The two climb out into a starless sky that slowly, painfully rekindles as freed souls return to memory. Ilsa chooses to report the truth rather than a tidy lie. Beat: exhausted hope.

chapters.title: The City That Outlawed Magic
chapters.summary: POV Freya. Freya returns powerless—no immunity, no charms—to a city facing the ledger of its own founding sin. He testifies publicly, not as hero but as evidence. Beat: justice begun, unfinished.

chapters.title: One Dish at a Time
chapters.summary: POV Freya, coda. Months later: Freya cooks in a small kitchen, Bryn relearning the world beside him, charms legal in a narrow licensed quarter. He tastes nothing dangerous anymore and finds ordinary food enough. Beat: peace earned, identity remade.
